The proposal targets multiple sections of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR), including parts 13, 47, 49, 61, 63, 65, 187, and 406, covering civil penalties, registration fees, and FAA services. FAA will revise associated guidance documents to direct electronic payments and allow alternative methods only where permitted by law. The goal is to standardize FAA’s payment processes, improve operational efficiency, and minimize customer costs while adhering to legal exceptions.

summary_responses.subtopic: Aerospace Rotorcraft Structural Engineering & FAA Airworthiness Directives
summary_responses.response: The FAA proposes a new airworthiness directive (AD) for Airbus EC135 and EC635T2+ helicopters, requiring inspections of the tail rotor control system after hard landings due to incomplete manufacturer instructions. This AD mandates a one-time inspection within 12 months of adoption and revisions to maintenance manuals or programs, depending on inspection results. It applies only to FAA-certified models, excluding those without a type certificate, and incorporates EASA guidelines with specific exceptions. Public comments must be received by January 4, 2027, via regulations.gov, fax, or mail to potentially amend the proposal. The directive aims to address an unsafe condition that could lead to undetected damage and system failures, ensuring aviation safety.

key_facts: The National Park Service final rule for Mammoth Cave National Park is effective December 21, 2026, and allows bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails.
The rule allows visitors to ride horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, expanding equestrian opportunities in the park.
Under the preferred alternative, the NPS will add approximately 66 miles of land-based trails to the park trail system, representing a 72 percent increase in trail mileage.

The rule adds eight new trails for bicycle use, including Brooks Knob Road Cemetery Trail, Brooks Knob Road Trail, Crystal Cave Road Trail, East Entrance Trail, Little Hope Cemetery Trail, Sugar Sink Connector Trail, Sugar Sink Trail, and West Entrance Trail.

In December 2024, the Regional Director for Interior Region 2, South Atlantic—Gulf, signed a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) selecting the preferred alternative from the Environmental Assessment.
The final rule opens the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road to horseback riding.
